purpose: Rollback baseline captured BEFORE any Direct Send phase-2 edit. These two version numbers are the rollback targets: point the `live` alias back at them if the deployed code itself is at fault. Note that the primary rollback is cheaper than that - clearing DIRECT_SEND_ENABLED_WABAS makes the request byte-identical to today, because an absent `category` key is Meta's own definition of a service message.
notes: Both functions are invoked through the `live` alias, so $LATEST does not reach production. A deploy is not live until a version is published and the alias moves.
Both aliases pointed at the same CodeSha256 as $LATEST at capture time, so there was no pre-existing undeployed drift to confuse a rollback.
Env key NAMES are recorded, never values. DIRECT_SEND_ENABLED_WABAS was absent on both functions before this change; the new value is an empty string, which is not a secret.
